title.en: Conditions that guarantee congruence (SSS, SAS, ASA)

text.en:
Raju cut two triangles from paper using the same three side lengths and they matched exactly.
"Three equal sides are enough," he said.

Two triangles are congruent if all matching sides and angles are equal, but we do not need all six. Three equal sides (SSS) are enough.
Two sides and the angle between them (SAS) are enough, and so are two angles and the side between them (ASA).
Two sides and an angle not between them (SSA) do not always guarantee congruence. Angles of an isosceles triangle opposite equal sides are equal.

SAS: two sides and the included angle.
ASA: two angles and the included side.

prompt.en: A friend says three equal angles always make congruent triangles. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Equal angles may give different sizes.
